item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":0,"rationale":"The President states policy findings and objectives but directs no agency action and creates no legal consequence.","evidence":"The development and implementation of transportation infrastructure projects in an efficient and environmentally sound manner is essential to the well-being of the American people and a strong American economy."},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"Agencies and the Secretary are directed to pursue, formulate, and implement administrative mechanisms and cooperative actions, with no specified legal outcome mandated.","evidence":"agencies shall, in support of the Department of Transportation, formulate and implement administrative, policy, and procedural mechanisms"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary must maintain an internal priority list, agencies must expedite reviews where practicable, and the order establishes and staffs an interagency coordinating body; later permit outcomes remain unspecified.","evidence":"There is established, within the Department of Transportation for administrative purposes, the interagency \"Transportation Infrastructure Streamlining Task Force\""},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The segment assigns an internal reporting channel from the Task Force to the President, without affecting legal rights or dictating an agency legal outcome.","evidence":"The Task Force shall report to the President through the Chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality."},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The Task Force must periodically report findings and recommendations to the President, while the remaining clauses preserve internal authority and disclaim enforceable rights; no substantive legal consequence is imposed.","evidence":"At least once each year, the Task Force shall submit to the President a report"}]}
